about: Published studies that used each dataset. Each entry was checked against the paper's own text. Set "reviewed" to true once you have checked an entry yourself.

early-cycle-life.coverage: A starting list of 9 papers, mostly picked from the most-cited work that cites Severson et al. (2019), which has over 3,000 citations. Not every paper that used this dataset.

papers.title: Data-driven prediction of battery cycle life before capacity degradation
papers.use: Introduces the dataset: 124 commercial LFP/graphite cells (A123 APR18650M1A) cycled under fast-charging conditions, with cycle lives from about 150 to 2,300 cycles.
papers.split: 41 training cells, 43 primary test cells, 40 secondary test cells. Later papers call this the original split.
papers.evidence: Abstract; split described in Attia et al. (2021), Table I

papers.title: Closed-loop optimization of fast-charging protocols for batteries with machine learning
papers.use: Uses the early-prediction model built on this dataset to shorten each experiment, then searches 224 six-step fast-charging protocols with Bayesian optimisation. The new cells it cycled are also published on data.matr.io.

papers.title: Statistical learning for accurate and interpretable battery lifetime prediction
papers.use: Re-analyses this dataset with simple, interpretable models and compares them with the original models and a CNN.
papers.split: Original split (41 / 43 / 40 cells), with one outlier cell removed from the primary test set.
papers.evidence: Summary of dataset and previous work; Table I; Table II

results.model: CNN on ΔQ(V), mean of 10 runs
log10 IQR of ΔQ100−10(V), one feature
CNN on ΔQ(V), mean of 10 runs
log10 IQR of ΔQ100−10(V), one feature

papers.title: Elbows of internal resistance rise curves in Li-ion cells
papers.use: Trains a model on the internal-resistance data of these 124 cells to fill in the missing resistance values for the 233 cells of Attia et al. (2020), then predicts the elbow point of resistance rise from early cycles.
papers.split: Resistance model trained on these 124 cells (batches 1–3) and applied to batches 4–8.

papers.title: Deep neural network battery life and voltage prediction by using data of one cycle only
papers.use: Uses 81 to 115 of the 124 cells, after removing cells with poor-quality data, to predict end of life, remaining life and voltage curves from as little as one cycle.
papers.split: Own split: 5-fold cross-validation (80/20), holding out whole cells or whole charging policies. Not the original split.

results.why: Their own random split of cells, after removing cells with poor data, not the original test sets.

papers.title: BatteryML: An open-source platform for machine learning on battery degradation
papers.authors: Zhang, Gui, Zheng, Lu, Li, Bian
papers.use: Packages this dataset, together with the Attia et al. (2020) cells, as the MATR benchmark and compares many models on it with fixed splits.
papers.split: MATR1 and MATR2 follow the original split (MATR2 tests on unseen charging policies); CLO is a random split.

results.why: Uses the original split, but the table gives no unit and does not say whether the outlier cell was removed. Its re-run of Severson's discharge model scored 329 on MATR1, against 86 in the original paper.

papers.title: Two points are enough
papers.use: Uses the 124 cells, plus 45 cells from Attia et al. (2020) as an extra test set, to show that a feature built from just two voltage points predicts cycle life about as well as published features.
papers.split: Original split (41 / 43 / 40 cells); the Attia et al. cells are used as a third test set.

papers.title: Physics-informed neural network for lithium-ion battery degradation stable modeling and prognosis
papers.use: One of four datasets used to test a physics-informed state-of-health model.
papers.split: Own split: cells divided about 6:2:2 into training, validation and test sets.

papers.title: Physical information-guided Kolmogorov–Arnold networks for battery state of health estimation
papers.use: Main dataset for a physics-informed KAN model that estimates state of health.
papers.split: Uses the original cell groups as 41 training, 40 validation and 43 test cells.

early-cycle-life.results_note: Numbers as reported in each paper, not re-run by IonSense. Only results on the same test cells and metric are ranked together. All ranked results use data from the first 100 cycles. Lower RMSE is better.

benchmarks.label: Primary test, all 43 cells
benchmarks.note: Includes the one primary-test cell that Severson et al. describe as an outlier.

benchmarks.label: Primary test, outlier cell removed (42 cells)
benchmarks.note: Severson et al. report this alongside the full set; Attia et al. (2021) use it throughout.

benchmarks.label: Secondary test, 40 cells
benchmarks.note: Cells charged with policies not seen in training, so this set is harder.

nasa-battery-data-set.coverage: A starting list of 5 studies. This is one of the most widely used battery datasets, so the list covers only a few of the papers that used it.

papers.title: Battery Data Set
papers.venue: NASA Prognostics Data Repository, NASA Ames Research Center
papers.use: Releases the data: Li-ion cells repeatedly charged and discharged at several ambient temperatures, with impedance measured along the way.
papers.evidence: NASA PCoE data repository, item 5 (citation given there)

papers.title: Transformer network for remaining useful life prediction of lithium-ion batteries
papers.use: Predicts remaining useful life from the capacity curves of cells B0005, B0006, B0007 and B0018, after denoising them with an autoencoder.
papers.split: Leave one battery out across the four cells.
papers.evidence: Abstract; companion code (github.com/XiuzeZhou/RUL) loads B0005, B0006, B0007 and B0018

papers.title: A framework for Li-ion battery prognosis based on hybrid Bayesian physics-informed neural networks
papers.use: Uses full discharges from this dataset to fit a hybrid physics-informed model and its ageing parameters, together with NASA's randomized-usage data.
papers.split: Predictions for batteries left out of training; battery IDs are not listed in the main text.
papers.evidence: Results; Data availability (NASA repository sets 5 and 11)

papers.title: SambaMixer: State of health prediction of Li-ion batteries using Mamba state space models
papers.use: Predicts state of health from discharge cycles of 19 batteries tested at 4, 24 and 43 °C.
papers.split: Tests on batteries #6, #7 and #47; three training sets of 4, 5 or 11 other batteries.
papers.evidence: Section V-A; Tables II and III

papers.title: State of health estimation for lithium-ion batteries based on transferable long short-term memory optimized using Harris hawk algorithm
papers.use: Pre-trains an LSTM model on cells B0006 and B0007, then transfers it to CALCE and XJTU cells.

identifying-degradation-patterns-via-imp.coverage: A starting list of 4 studies, found by searching for papers that reuse these 12 coin cells. Not every paper that used this dataset.

papers.title: Identifying degradation patterns of lithium ion batteries from impedance spectroscopy using machine learning
papers.use: Introduces the dataset: more than 20,000 impedance spectra from 12 LiCoO2/graphite coin cells (Eunicell LR2032) cycled at 25, 35 and 45 °C.
papers.split: 6 training cells (25C01–25C04, 35C01, 45C01) and 6 test cells (25C05–25C08, 35C02, 45C02).

papers.title: Impedance-based capacity estimation for lithium-ion batteries using generative adversarial network
papers.use: Uses the 8 cells cycled at 25 °C to learn features from the spectra without labels, then estimates capacity from them.
papers.split: 25C01–25C04 for training, 25C05–25C08 for testing.

papers.title: Feature extraction from electrochemical impedance spectroscopy for state of health estimation of lithium-ion batteries under different temperatures
papers.use: Picks the single most informative impedance feature by correlation and uses it to estimate state of health at all three temperatures.
papers.split: Tested on cells 25C05, 35C02 and 45C02.
papers.evidence: Section II (Battery data sets); Sections III and IV

papers.title: Two points are enough
papers.use: Estimates capacity from the impedance at just two frequencies and compares this with the original study's features.
papers.split: Same 6 / 6 cell split as the original study.

identifying-degradation-patterns-via-imp.results_note: No ranked results yet. The studies report different metrics on different cells: the original paper gives R² only inside its figures, Liu et al. (IPEMC 2024) give MAPE per cell, and Kim et al. and Liu et al. (2024 preprint) use subsets of the test cells.

data-driven-capacity-estimation-from-vol.coverage: A starting list of 5 studies, found by searching for papers that reuse these 130 cells. Not every paper that used this dataset.

papers.title: Data-driven capacity estimation of commercial lithium-ion batteries from voltage relaxation
papers.use: Introduces the dataset: 130 commercial 18650 cells in three chemistries (NCA, NCM and an NCM+NCA blend) cycled at 25, 35 and 45 °C, with the voltage relaxation after every full charge.
papers.split: Split by cell, about 4:1, so no cell is in both training and test. The NCM and blend cells test transfer to new chemistries.

papers.title: Long short-term memory network with transfer learning for lithium-ion battery capacity fade and cycle life prediction
papers.use: Pre-trains a model on the NCA cells' capacity curves, then adapts it to NCM cells with very little data to predict capacity fade and cycle life.
papers.split: Pre-trained on 20 NCA cells (25 and 45 °C), retrained on 2 NCM cells at 25 °C, tested on 10 NCM cells at 45 °C.
papers.evidence: Section 2 (Data acquisition), which points to Zhu et al. (2022) for the data

papers.title: Comprehensive performance comparison among different types of features in data-driven battery state of health estimation
papers.use: Compares equivalent-circuit, statistical and raw-voltage features of the relaxation curve on 118 of the cells.
papers.split: Several splits compared: half the cells per condition, random ratios, leave one temperature out, and first 80% / last 20% of cycles.
papers.evidence: Section II (Data generation); Table I; Section IV.B

papers.title: Two points are enough
papers.use: Estimates capacity from two points of the relaxation voltage and compares this with the original study's three statistical features.

papers.title: Physics-informed neural network for lithium-ion battery degradation stable modeling and prognosis
papers.use: One of four datasets used to test a physics-informed state-of-health model (called the TJU dataset there).
papers.split: Cells divided about 6:2:2 into training, validation and test sets.

battery-failure-databank-nrel.coverage: A starting list of 4 studies, found by searching for papers that use the databank. Not every paper that used it.

papers.title: The battery failure databank: Insights from an open-access database of thermal runaway behaviors of Li-ion cells and a resource for benchmarking risks
papers.use: Describes the databank and analyses 364 fractional thermal runaway calorimetry tests on 18650, 21700 and D-cell formats, some with high-speed X-ray videos.

papers.title: Thermal runaway of Li-ion cells: how internal dynamics, mass ejection and heat vary with cell geometry and abuse type
papers.use: Compares heat output, mass ejection and internal dynamics across four cell models from the databank under nail, heater and internal-short tests.

papers.title: Predicting the heat release variability of Li-ion cells under thermal runaway with few or no calorimetry data
papers.use: Uses 139 calorimetry tests on 8 cell types (databank version 2) to predict how much heat a cell releases, from ejected mass and the manufacturer's specifications.
papers.split: One cell type held out at a time, with none or a few of its tests added to training.
papers.evidence: Results (Training data); Methods (Data collection, Data pre-processing)

papers.title: Thermal runaway diagnosis of lithium-ion cells using data-driven method
papers.use: Classifies the cause of thermal runaway (heater, internal short or nail) from 26 measured features of the 364 tests.
papers.split: 80:20 split (291 training, 73 test tests) and 10-fold cross-validation.

lithium-ion-battery-aging-dataset-based-.coverage: A starting list of 4 studies, found by searching for papers that reuse these cells. Not every paper that used this dataset.

papers.title: Lithium-ion battery aging dataset based on electric vehicle real-driving profiles
papers.use: Introduces the dataset: 10 NMC/graphite-silicon 21700 cells (INR21700-M50T) discharged with repeated UDDS driving cycles, with periodic capacity, HPPC and impedance tests.
papers.evidence: Data article; cell details as reported by Lanubile et al. (2024) and Wang et al. (2025)

papers.title: Domain knowledge-guided machine learning framework for state of health estimation in lithium-ion batteries
papers.use: Uses 5 of the 10 cells to build health indicators that can be computed from battery-management signals while driving and charging, then estimates state of health.
papers.split: Trained on one cell, or on all cells but the test cell.
papers.evidence: Data section (cites Pozzato et al. 2022); Results

papers.title: Capacity estimation of lithium-ion batteries using invariance property in open circuit voltage relationship
papers.use: Uses cell W5 to test a capacity estimate based on the open-circuit-voltage curve keeping its shape as the cell ages.
papers.split: Single cell: OCV checks at cycles 159 to 344 and 12 driving cycles.
papers.evidence: Section 3 (3.1 OCV test data, 3.2 dynamic discharge data)

papers.title: Second-life lithium-ion battery aging dataset based on grid storage cycling
papers.authors: Moy, Khan, Fasolato, Pozzato, Allam, Onori
papers.use: Takes six of these cells after their EV-driving ageing and continues ageing them for 24 months on grid-storage duty cycles.
papers.evidence: Data article abstract (cells previously tested for 23 months on a UDDS profile)

aging-dataset-lco-battery-with-mechanica.coverage: 2 studies, both from the group that made the dataset. No use by other groups found yet; the data was released in February 2025.

papers.title: Aging diagnostics in lithium-ion batteries with differential mechanical measurements
papers.use: Introduces the data: an LCO/graphite cell cycled over 1,000 times to 70% state of health, with its thickness change split into a reversible part within each cycle and an irreversible part that grows with ageing.
papers.evidence: Abstract; Zenodo record links this paper

papers.title: Mechanics of lithium-ion batteries: aging and diagnostics
papers.use: Review that reuses the LCO ageing test for deformation-based state-of-charge estimation, differential expansion diagnostics and validation of the group's coupled ageing model.
papers.evidence: Section 2.2 (same protocol: C/2 charge, 1C discharge, 20 °C, reference tests every 25 cycles); Figures 3, 5, 6 and 10

uconn-lco-gr-battery-fast-charging-datas.coverage: 1 study, the one that produced the data. No other use found yet; the dataset was released in January 2026.

papers.title: Coulombic efficiency-driven optimization of health-aware charging protocols: an experimental investigation on LCO/graphite lithium-ion cells
papers.authors: Navidi, Das, Nowacki, Shrotriya, Xu, Hu
papers.use: Measures coulombic efficiency across state of charge, charge rate and health, then designs fast-charging protocols that limit capacity fade, benchmarked against constant-current constant-voltage charging.
papers.evidence: Abstract; dataset page cites Navidi et al. for the protocols

tum-commercial-aging.coverage: A starting list of 4 studies, found by searching for papers that reuse these 196 cells. Not every paper that used this dataset.

papers.title: Experimental degradation study of a commercial lithium-ion battery
papers.authors: Wildfeuer, Karger, Aygül, Wassiliadis, Jossen, Lienkamp
papers.use: Introduces the dataset: calendar and cyclic ageing of commercial NCA / silicon-graphite 18650 cells under many storage and cycling conditions.
papers.evidence: Cited as the source of the data by Philipp et al. (2026, ref. 24) and Liu et al. (2024, ref. 22); the paper itself could not be opened here

papers.title: Two points are enough
papers.use: Estimates state of health from two points of the relaxation voltage after discharge, compared with the statistical features of Zhu et al. (2022).
papers.split: Random split by cell: 157 cells for training, 39 for testing.

papers.title: Physics-based modeling of cyclic and calendar aging of LIBs with Si-Gr composite anodes
papers.authors: Philipp, Köbbing, Karger, Jossen, Latz, Horstmann
papers.use: Builds a physics-based ageing model that separates SEI growth from silicon-specific effects and checks it against the calendar and cyclic ageing data.
papers.evidence: Section II A (Experimental data); Table I

papers.title: Discovery Learning predicts battery cycle life from minimal experiments
papers.use: One of the public datasets (Sony VTC5A cells from TUM) used to train a model that predicts the cycle life of new cell designs.
papers.evidence: Data availability (lists Sony-VTC5A from the Technical University of Munich)

full-factorial-doe-dataset-for-parallel-.coverage: 2 papers from the team that made the dataset. The data article is cited about 14 times, but no reuse by other groups was confirmed yet.

papers.title: Full factorial design of experiments dataset for parallel-connected lithium-ion cells imbalanced performance investigation
papers.use: Describes the 54 module tests on four parallel-connected cells and the single-cell characterisation of 39 cells.
papers.evidence: Data article (Experimental design, materials and methods)

papers.title: Unveiling the performance impact of module level features on parallel-connected lithium-ion cells via explainable machine learning techniques on a full factorial design of experiments
papers.use: Finds which module features drive uneven current, state of charge and temperature across parallel cells; interconnection resistance matters most.

physics-informed-neural-network-for-lith.coverage: A starting list of 5 studies. The dataset's authors keep a much longer list of papers that use it, with their reported results.
physics-informed-neural-network-for-lith.more_label: Full list kept by the dataset authors

papers.title: Physics-informed neural network for lithium-ion battery degradation stable modeling and prognosis
papers.use: Introduces the XJTU dataset and estimates state of health with a physics-informed neural network, tested on it and on three public datasets (Zhu et al. 2022, Ma et al. 2022, Severson et al. 2019).
papers.split: Cells split about 6:2:2 into training, validation and test sets within each dataset; 10 repeats.

papers.title: Open access dataset, code library and benchmarking deep learning approaches for state-of-health estimation of lithium-ion batteries
papers.use: Benchmarks CNN, LSTM, GRU, MLP and attention models for state-of-health estimation on all 55 cells.
papers.split: Train and test on different cells.
papers.evidence: Listed with results in the dataset authors' summary of papers; the article itself was not opened here

papers.title: Integrated mixed attention U-Net mechanisms with multi-stage division strategy customized for accurate estimation of lithium-ion battery state of health
papers.use: Estimates state of health on batches 1 to 3 with an attention U-Net, after splitting each degradation curve into stages at its knee point.
papers.split: Leave one cell out within each batch.

papers.title: State of health estimation for lithium-ion batteries based on transferable long short-term memory optimized using Harris hawk algorithm
papers.use: Transfers an LSTM model pre-trained on NASA cells to the first cell of batch 1.
papers.split: Single cell (batch 1, cell 1): fine-tuned on its first 30% of data, or trained on its first 70%.
papers.evidence: Section 2 (datasets); split as summarised in the dataset authors' list of papers

papers.title: Physical information-guided Kolmogorov–Arnold networks for battery state of health estimation
papers.use: Uses batches 1 to 4 to test how well a physics-informed KAN model, developed on the Severson et al. cells, generalises.

discovery-learning-predicts-battery-cycl.coverage: 1 study, the one that produced the data. The dataset was released in late 2025, so no reuse yet.

papers.title: Discovery Learning predicts battery cycle life from minimal experiments
papers.use: Predicts the cycle life of new cell designs from the first cycles of about half of the prototypes, after learning from public datasets of other designs.

lithium-inventory-tracking-as-a-nondestr.coverage: 1 study, the one that produced the data. No use by other groups found yet.

papers.title: Lithium inventory tracking as a non-destructive battery evaluation and monitoring method
papers.use: Converts measured capacity into an estimate of active lithium in the electrode, and tracks it from formation to end of life in lithium-metal / NMC811 cells.

gic-nmc-solar-battery-synthetic-data.coverage: 1 study, the one that produced the data. A 2023 follow-up by the same group generates new synthetic data with the same method rather than reusing this set.

papers.title: Data-driven direct diagnosis of Li-ion batteries connected to photovoltaics
papers.use: Trains models on the synthetic data to identify degradation modes (lithium inventory loss and active material loss on each electrode) in solar-charged batteries.

battery-aging-modes-across-nmc-compositi.coverage: 1 study, the one that produced the data. No use by other groups found yet.

papers.title: Battery aging mode identification across NMC compositions and designs using machine learning
papers.authors: Chen, Walker, Kim, Kunz, Tanim, Dufek
papers.use: Classifies the main ageing mode of each cell (lithium plating, SEI growth, cathode material loss) from cycle-by-cycle signals, and estimates cathode material loss.

comprehensive-battery-aging-dataset-nmc-.coverage: 2 studies found so far. Not every paper that used this dataset.

papers.title: Comprehensive battery aging dataset: capacity and impedance fade measurements of a lithium-ion NMC/C-SiO cell
papers.use: Describes the 228-cell ageing campaign: calendar, cycling and driving-profile ageing at four temperatures, with capacity, impedance and pulse check-ups.

papers.title: Estimation of the state of charge and health of lithium-ion batteries based on deep learning
papers.use: Estimates state of charge and state of health from voltage, current and temperature windows.
papers.split: State of health: whole ageing conditions held out for testing.

cycle-aging-data-of-automotive-grade-li-.coverage: 1 study, the one that produced the data. The dataset was released in 2025, so no reuse yet.

papers.title: Understanding lithium-ion battery degradation in vehicle applications: Insights from realistic and accelerated aging tests using Volkswagen ID.3 pouch cells
papers.authors: Schreiber, Abo Gamra, Bilfinger et al.
papers.use: Compares three years of realistic highway and commuting profiles with an accelerated 1C/1C test, and with a pack in a test vehicle. Accelerated testing over-predicted lithium loss compared with commuting use.

second-life-lithium-ion-battery-aging-da.coverage: 1 study, the one that produced the data. No use by other groups found yet.

papers.title: Second-life lithium-ion battery aging dataset based on grid storage cycling
papers.authors: Moy, Khan, Fasolato, Pozzato, Allam, Onori
papers.use: Continues ageing six cells from the EV real-driving profile dataset on grid-storage duty cycles, to see whether used EV cells suit second-life storage.
